content.text:
Map each node in every diagram on the provided canvas to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change any diagram’s text or the canvas layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (terminal):
Map d5 all nodes. Read relevant ranges with line numbers. Return JSON mappings; cover declarations fully as requested.

1	//! Maintains a linked list of pages to make up a terminal screen
     2	//! and provides higher level operations on top of those pages to
     3	//! make it slightly easier to work with.
     4	const PageList = @This();
     5	
     6	const std = @import("std");
     7	const builtin = @import("builtin");
     8	const build_options = @import("terminal_options");
     9	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
    10	const assert = @import("../quirks.zig").inlineAssert;
    11	const fastmem = @import("../fastmem.zig");
    12	const simd = @import("../simd/main.zig");
    13	const tripwire = @import("../tripwire.zig");
    14	const DoublyLinkedList = @import("../datastruct/main.zig").IntrusiveDoublyLinkedList;
    15	const datastruct = @import("../datastruct/main.zig");
    16	const color = @import("color.zig");
    17	const compression = @import("compress.zig");
    18	const highlight = @import("highlight.zig");
    19	const hyperlink = @import("hyperlink.zig");
    20	const kitty = @import("kitty.zig");
    21	const terminal_mem = @import("mem.zig");
    22	const point = @import("point.zig");
    23	const pagepkg = @import("page.zig");
    24	const stylepkg = @import("style.zig");
    25	const size = @import("size.zig");
    26	const OffsetBuf = size.OffsetBuf;
    27	const Capacity = pagepkg.Capacity;
    28	const Page = pagepkg.Page;
    29	const Row = pagepkg.Row;
    30	
    31	const log = std.log.scoped(.page_list);
    32	const native_freestanding = builtin.target.os.tag == .freestanding and
    33	    !builtin.target.cpu.arch.isWasm();
    34	
    35	/// The number of pages we preheat the page pool with. For operating systems
    36	/// that support it, pages are demand-paged (see PagePool) so this only
    37	/// costs us address space. For other operating systems, we don't preheat.
    38	const page_preheat = 4;
    39	
    40	/// The number of nodes we preheat the node pool with. Unlike pages, nodes
    41	/// are ordinary heap memory so every idle preheated node costs real
    42	/// memory. A new PageList needs exactly one node for its first page, so
    43	/// we preheat that one and let the pool grow on demand.
    44	const node_preheat = 1;
    45	
    46	/// The number of pins we preheat the pin pool with: the viewport pin that
    47	/// every PageList tracks and the cursor pin that every Screen tracks.
    48	/// Selections, searches, and so on grow the pool on demand.
    49	const pin_preheat = 2;
    50	
    51	/// The list of pages in the screen. These are expected to be in order
    52	/// where the first page is the topmost page (scrollback) and the last is
    53	/// the bottommost page (the current active page).
    54	pub const List = DoublyLinkedList(Node);
    55	
    56	/// A single node within the PageList linked list.
    57	///
    58	/// This isn't pub because you can access the type via List.Node.
    59	const Node = struct {
    60	    prev: ?*Node = null,
    61	    next: ?*Node = null,
    62	    data: Data,
    63	    serial: u64,
    64	
    65	    /// How the backing memory of the embedded Page was allocated. Pool-owned
    66	    /// memory is always a full standard-size item from the memory
    67	    /// pool, regardless of the page layout size. Heap-owned memory
    68	    /// is allocated directly with the page allocator and is exactly
    69	    /// `Page.memory.len` bytes.
    70	    ///
    71	    /// This must never be inferred from the memory length: heap-owned
    72	    /// pages can be smaller than the standard size (e.g. compacted
    73	    /// pages), and returning one to the pool would corrupt it.
    74	    ///
    75	    /// This has no default on purpose so that every construction site
    76	    /// is forced to make an explicit decision.
    77	    owned: Owned,
    78	
    79	    /// The physical representation of the page contents.
    80	    ///
    81	    /// Both states retain the same `Page.memory` virtual mapping and the same
    82	    /// `Page` metadata. A resident page can access the mapping directly since
    83	    /// it is, well, resident.
    84	    ///
    85	    /// A compressed page owns an encoded copy while the physical memory
    86	    /// behind the raw mapping is discarded. HOWEVER, we retain the
    87	    /// virtual allocation so that restoration is infallible.
    88	    const Data = union(enum) {
    89	        resident: Page,
    90	        compressed: compression.Page,
    91	    };
    92	
    93	    const Owned = enum { pool, heap };
    94	
    95	    /// The backing-memory representation currently stored by this node.
    96	    pub const Storage = enum { resident, compressed };
    97	
    98	    /// Return the terminal page stored in this node.
    99	    ///
   100	    /// WARNING: This will DECOMPRESS compressed pages! Only use this if
   101	    /// you need access to the underlying memory. If you only need access to
   102	    /// metadata (row, col counts etc) then use the other metadata functions.
   103	    pub inline fn page(self: *Node) *Page {
   104	        return switch (self.data) {
   105	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   106	            .compressed => self.restore(.preserve),
   107	        };
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    /// Return the terminal page only when its raw memory is resident.
   111	    ///
   112	    /// Unlike `page`, this never restores a compressed node. This is useful
   113	    /// for diagnostics which can display node metadata without touching the
   114	    /// discarded mapping, but may inspect page contents when they are already
   115	    /// available.
   116	    pub inline fn pageIfResident(self: *Node) ?*Page {
   117	        return switch (self.data) {
   118	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   119	            .compressed => null,
   120	        };
   121	    }
   122	
   123	    /// Read-only page with full memory access that doesn't change
   124	    /// this node's storage state: if a node is compressed it remains
   125	    /// compressed.
   126	    ///
   127	    /// Resident pages are borrowed directly. So they're basically free.
   128	    ///
   129	    /// Compressed pages are decoded into an independently owned Page
   130	    /// by the caller so callers can inspect their contents. Because resident
   131	    /// pages are still borrowed, you have to continue to have exclusive
   132	    /// access to the PageList during this operation.
   133	    pub const PreservedPage = union(enum) {
   134	        borrowed: *const Page,
   135	        owned: struct {
   136	            page: Page,
   137	            alloc: Allocator,
   138	        },
   139	
   140	        /// Return the read-only page represented by this value.
   141	        pub fn page(self: *const PreservedPage) *const Page {
   142	            return switch (self.*) {
   143	                .borrowed => |page_| page_,
   144	                .owned => |*owned| &owned.page,
   145	            };
   146	        }
   147	
   148	        /// Release storage owned by this preserved page.
   149	        pub fn deinit(self: *PreservedPage) void {
   150	            switch (self.*) {
   151	                .borrowed => {},
   152	                // The clone buffer came from the caller's allocator rather
   153	                // than Page's OS allocator, so it must not use Page.deinit.
   154	                .owned => |*owned| owned.alloc.free(owned.page.memory),
   155	            }
   156	            self.* = undefined;
   157	        }
   158	    };
   159	
   160	    /// Return read-only page contents without changing this node's storage.
   161	    ///
   162	    /// `alloc` is unused for a resident node. A compressed node uses it for an
   163	    /// exact-sized, page-aligned decode buffer owned by the returned value.
   164	    ///
   165	    /// The caller must call `PreservedPage.deinit` when finished. See
   166	    /// `PreservedPage` for the synchronization required by its borrowed
   167	    /// resident representation.
   168	    pub fn pagePreservingState(
   169	        self: *const Node,
   170	        alloc: Allocator,
   171	    ) Allocator.Error!PreservedPage {
   172	        return switch (self.data) {
   173	            .resident => |*page_| .{ .borrowed = page_ },
   174	            .compressed => |*compressed| owned: {
   175	                const memory = try alloc.alignedAlloc(
   176	                    u8,
   177	                    .fromByteUnits(std.heap.page_size_min),
   178	                    compressed.page.memory.len,
   179	                );
   180	
   181	                const page_ = compressed.cloneBuf(memory) catch |err| {

   183	                    // immutable while compressed. Failure is internal

    96	    pub const Storage = enum { resident, compressed };
    97	
    98	    /// Return the terminal page stored in this node.
    99	    ///
   100	    /// WARNING: This will DECOMPRESS compressed pages! Only use this if
   101	    /// you need access to the underlying memory. If you only need access to
   102	    /// metadata (row, col counts etc) then use the other metadata functions.
   103	    pub inline fn page(self: *Node) *Page {
   104	        return switch (self.data) {
   105	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   106	            .compressed => self.restore(.preserve),
   107	        };
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    /// Return the terminal page only when its raw memory is resident.
   111	    ///
   112	    /// Unlike `page`, this never restores a compressed node. This is useful
   113	    /// for diagnostics which can display node metadata without touching the
   114	    /// discarded mapping, but may inspect page contents when they are already
   115	    /// available.
   116	    pub inline fn pageIfResident(self: *Node) ?*Page {
   117	        return switch (self.data) {
   118	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   119	            .compressed => null,
   120	        };
   121	    }
   122	
   123	    /// Read-only page with full memory access that doesn't change
   124	    /// this node's storage state: if a node is compressed it remains
   125	    /// compressed.
   126	    ///
   127	    /// Resident pages are borrowed directly. So they're basically free.
   128	    ///
   129	    /// Compressed pages are decoded into an independently owned Page
   130	    /// by the caller so callers can inspect their contents. Because resident
   131	    /// pages are still borrowed, you have to continue to have exclusive
   132	    /// access to the PageList during this operation.
   133	    pub const PreservedPage = union(enum) {
   134	        borrowed: *const Page,
   135	        owned: struct {
   136	            page: Page,
   137	            alloc: Allocator,
   138	        },
   139	
   140	        /// Return the read-only page represented by this value.
   141	        pub fn page(self: *const PreservedPage) *const Page {
   142	            return switch (self.*) {
   143	                .borrowed => |page_| page_,
   144	                .owned => |*owned| &owned.page,
   145	            };
   146	        }
   147	
   148	        /// Release storage owned by this preserved page.
   149	        pub fn deinit(self: *PreservedPage) void {
   150	            switch (self.*) {
   151	                .borrowed => {},

   153	                // than Page's OS allocator, so it must not use Page.deinit.
   154	                .owned => |*owned| owned.alloc.free(owned.page.memory),
   155	            }

   157	        }
   158	    };

   160	    /// Return read-only page contents without changing this node's storage.
   161	    ///
   162	    /// `alloc` is unused for a resident node. A compressed node uses it for an
   163	    /// exact-sized, page-aligned decode buffer owned by the returned value.
   164	    ///
   165	    /// The caller must call `PreservedPage.deinit` when finished. See
   166	    /// `PreservedPage` for the synchronization required by its borrowed
   167	    /// resident representation.
   168	    pub fn pagePreservingState(

   170	        alloc: Allocator,
   171	    ) Allocator.Error!PreservedPage {
   172	        return switch (self.data) {

   174	            .compressed => |*compressed| owned: {

   176	                    u8,
   177	                    .fromByteUnits(std.heap.page_size_min),
   178	                    compressed.page.memory.len,
   179	                );

   181	                const page_ = compressed.cloneBuf(memory) catch |err| {

   183	                    // immutable while compressed. Failure is internal
   184	                    // corruption, matching the normal restoration boundary.
   185	                    switch (err) {

   187	                        error.InvalidOffset,
   188	                        error.OutputTooSmall,
   189	                        error.OutputSizeMismatch,
   190	                        => {},
   191	                    }
   192	
   193	                    alloc.free(memory);
   194	                    log.err("failed to clone compressed page err={}", .{err});
   195	                    @panic("failed to clone compressed terminal page");
   196	                };

   198	                break :owned .{ .owned = .{
   199	                    .page = page_,
   200	                    .alloc = alloc,
   201	                } };
   202	            },
   203	        };
   204	    }
   205	
   206	    /// Return the node's backing-memory representation without restoring it.
   207	    pub inline fn storage(self: *const Node) Storage {
   208	        return switch (self.data) {
   209	            .resident => .resident,
   210	            .compressed => .compressed,
   211	        };
   212	    }
   213	
   214	    /// Return a page which the caller knows is already resident.
   215	    ///
   216	    /// This avoids the representation check in hot paths which already hold
   217	    /// live pointers into the page mapping. Such pointers are only valid while
   218	    /// the page is resident. Prefer `page` unless the caller can establish
   219	    /// that invariant independently.
   220	    pub inline fn pageAssumeResident(self: *Node) *Page {
   221	        return &self.data.resident;
   222	    }
   223	
   224	    /// Return the number of populated rows without accessing page memory.
   225	    pub inline fn rows(self: *const Node) size.CellCountInt {
   226	        return self.metadata().size.rows;
   227	    }
   228	
   229	    /// Return the current column count without accessing page memory.
   230	    pub inline fn cols(self: *const Node) size.CellCountInt {
   231	        return self.metadata().size.cols;
   232	    }
   233	
   234	    /// Return the page capacity without accessing page memory.
   235	    pub inline fn capacity(self: *const Node) Capacity {
   236	        return self.metadata().capacity;
   237	    }
   238	
   239	    /// Return the embedded Page metadata without restoring its memory.
   240	    inline fn metadata(self: *const Node) *const Page {
   241	        return switch (self.data) {
   242	            .resident => |*page_| page_,
   243	            .compressed => |*page_| &page_.page,
   244	        };
   245	    }
   246	
   247	    const RestoreMode = enum {
   248	        /// Decode the compressed representation back into the raw mapping.
   249	        preserve,
   250	
   251	        /// Discard the compressed representation without decoding it. The
   252	        /// caller must not read the page contents before overwriting them.
   253	        discard,
   254	    };
   255	
   256	    /// Restore this node to the resident representation.
   257	    ///
   258	    /// Preserve mode reconstructs the page contents and is used by `page`.
   259	    /// Discard mode skips decoding for callers which will overwrite or destroy
   260	    /// the page. Both modes recommit the retained mapping, free the encoded
   261	    /// allocation, and leave the node in a valid resident state.
   262	    noinline fn restore(self: *Node, comptime mode: RestoreMode) *Page {

   264	            .resident => |*page_| return page_,

   266	        };

   268	        // Decommit only discarded the physical pages. Recommit prepares the
   269	        // still-reserved mapping for decoding or reuse by the caller.
   270	        terminal_mem.recommit(compressed.page.memory);

   272	        const restored = switch (mode) {
   273	            .preserve => compressed.restore() catch |err| {

   275	                // output mapping used to create them. Any decode error is an
   276	                // internal codec bug or memory corruption. Keep this switch
   277	                // exhaustive so new decoder errors require classification.

   279	                    error.TruncatedInput,
   280	                    error.InvalidOffset,
   281	                    error.OutputTooSmall,
   282	                    error.OutputSizeMismatch,
   283	                    => {},
   284	                }
   285	
   286	                log.err("failed to restore compressed page err={}", .{err});
   287	                @panic("failed to restore compressed terminal page");
   288	            },
   289	
   290	            .discard => compressed.page,
   291	        };
   292	
   293	        // Remove our compressed data
   294	        compressed.deinit();
   295	
   296	        // We're now a resident, non-compressed node.
   297	        self.data = .{ .resident = restored };
   298	        return &self.data.resident;
   299	    }
   300	
   301	    inline fn isCompressed(self: *const Node) bool {
   302	        return switch (self.data) {
   303	            .resident => false,
   304	            .compressed => true,
   305	        };

1	//! Maintains a linked list of pages to make up a terminal screen
     2	//! and provides higher level operations on top of those pages to
     3	//! make it slightly easier to work with.
     4	const PageList = @This();
     5	
     6	const std = @import("std");
     7	const builtin = @import("builtin");
     8	const build_options = @import("terminal_options");
     9	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
    10	const assert = @import("../quirks.zig").inlineAssert;
    11	const fastmem = @import("../fastmem.zig");
    12	const simd = @import("../simd/main.zig");
    13	const tripwire = @import("../tripwire.zig");
    14	const DoublyLinkedList = @import("../datastruct/main.zig").IntrusiveDoublyLinkedList;
    15	const datastruct = @import("../datastruct/main.zig");
    16	const color = @import("color.zig");
    17	const compression = @import("compress.zig");
    18	const highlight = @import("highlight.zig");
    19	const hyperlink = @import("hyperlink.zig");
    20	const kitty = @import("kitty.zig");
    21	const terminal_mem = @import("mem.zig");
    22	const point = @import("point.zig");
    23	const pagepkg = @import("page.zig");
    24	const stylepkg = @import("style.zig");
    25	const size = @import("size.zig");
    26	const OffsetBuf = size.OffsetBuf;
    27	const Capacity = pagepkg.Capacity;
    28	const Page = pagepkg.Page;
    29	const Row = pagepkg.Row;
    30	
    31	const log = std.log.scoped(.page_list);
    32	const native_freestanding = builtin.target.os.tag == .freestanding and
    33	    !builtin.target.cpu.arch.isWasm();
    34	
    35	/// The number of pages we preheat the page pool with. For operating systems
    36	/// that support it, pages are demand-paged (see PagePool) so this only
    37	/// costs us address space. For other operating systems, we don't preheat.
    38	const page_preheat = 4;
    39	
    40	/// The number of nodes we preheat the node pool with. Unlike pages, nodes
    41	/// are ordinary heap memory so every idle preheated node costs real
    42	/// memory. A new PageList needs exactly one node for its first page, so
    43	/// we preheat that one and let the pool grow on demand.
    44	const node_preheat = 1;
    45	
    46	/// The number of pins we preheat the pin pool with: the viewport pin that
    47	/// every PageList tracks and the cursor pin that every Screen tracks.
    48	/// Selections, searches, and so on grow the pool on demand.
    49	const pin_preheat = 2;
    50	
    51	/// The list of pages in the screen. These are expected to be in order

365	    pins: PinPool,

   367	    pub const ResetMode = std.heap.ArenaAllocator.ResetMode;
   368	
   369	    pub fn init(
   370	        gen_alloc: Allocator,
   371	        page_alloc: Allocator,
   372	        preheat: usize,
   373	    ) Allocator.Error!MemoryPool {
   374	        var node_pool = try NodePool.initCapacity(gen_alloc, gen_alloc, node_preheat);
   375	        errdefer node_pool.deinit();
   376	        var page_pool = try PagePool.initCapacity(gen_alloc, page_alloc, preheat);
   377	        errdefer page_pool.deinit();
   378	        var pin_pool = try PinPool.initCapacity(gen_alloc, pin_preheat);
   379	        errdefer pin_pool.deinit();
   380	        return .{
   381	            .alloc = gen_alloc,
   382	            .nodes = node_pool,
   383	            .pages = page_pool,
   384	            .pins = pin_pool,
   385	        };
   386	    }
   387	
   388	    pub fn deinit(self: *MemoryPool) void {
   389	        self.pages.deinit();
   390	        self.nodes.deinit();
   391	        self.pins.deinit(self.alloc);
   392	    }
   393

   535	/// Calculates the initial capacity for a new page for a given column
   536	/// count. This will attempt to fit within std_size at all times so we
   537	/// can use our memory pool, but if cols is too big, this will return a
   538	/// larger capacity.
   539	///
   540	/// The returned capacity is always guaranteed to layout properly (not
   541	/// overflow). We are able to support capacities up to the maximum int
   542	/// value of cols, so this will never overflow.
   543	fn initialCapacity(cols: size.CellCountInt) Capacity {
   544	    // This is an important invariant that ensures that this function
   545	    // can never return an error. We verify here that our standard capacity
   546	    // when increased to maximum possible columns can always support at
   547	    // least one row in memory.
   548	    //
   549	    // IF THIS EVER FAILS: We probably need to modify our logic below
   550	    // to reduce other elements of the capacity (styles, graphemes, etc.).
   551	    // But, instead, I recommend taking a step back and re-evaluating
   552	    // life choices.
   553	    comptime {
   554	        var cap = std_capacity;
   555	        cap.cols = std.math.maxInt(size.CellCountInt);
   556	        const layout = Page.layout(cap);
   557	        assert(layout.total_size <= size.max_page_size);
   558	    }
   559	
   560	    if (std_capacity.adjust(
   561	        .{ .cols = cols },
   562	    )) |cap| {
   563	        // If we can adjust our standard capacity, we fit within the
   564	        // standard size and we're good!
   565	        return cap;
   566	    } else |err| {
   567	        // Ensure our error set doesn't change.
   568	        comptime assert(@TypeOf(err) == error{OutOfMemory});
   569	    }
   570	
   571	    // This code path means that our standard capacity can't even
   572	    // accommodate our column count! The only solution is to increase
   573	    // our capacity and go non-standard.
   574	    var cap: Capacity = std_capacity;
   575	    cap.cols = cols;
   576	    return cap;
   577	}

   580	///
   581	/// `alloc` is the caller-provided allocator. It is used on native freestanding
   582	/// targets, where no OS page allocator is available. Other targets select a
   583	/// platform-specific allocator below.
   584	inline fn pageAllocator(alloc: Allocator) Allocator {
   585	    // In tests we use our testing allocator so we can detect leaks.
   586	    if (builtin.is_test) return std.testing.allocator;
   587	
   588	    // Native freestanding targets don't have an OS page allocator, so use
   589	    // the allocator provided by the embedder.
   590	    if (native_freestanding) return alloc;
   591	
   592	    // On non-macOS we use our standard Zig page allocator.
   593	    if (!builtin.target.os.tag.isDarwin()) return std.heap.page_allocator;
   594	
   595	    // On macOS we want to tag our memory so we can assign it to our
   596	    // core terminal usage.
   597	    const mach = @import("../os/mach.zig");
   598	    return mach.taggedPageAllocator(.application_specific_1);
   599	}

   535	/// Calculates the initial capacity for a new page for a given column
   536	/// count. This will attempt to fit within std_size at all times so we
   537	/// can use our memory pool, but if cols is too big, this will return a
   538	/// larger capacity.
   539	///
   540	/// The returned capacity is always guaranteed to layout properly (not
   541	/// overflow). We are able to support capacities up to the maximum int
   542	/// value of cols, so this will never overflow.
   543	fn initialCapacity(cols: size.CellCountInt) Capacity {
   544	    // This is an important invariant that ensures that this function
   545	    // can never return an error. We verify here that our standard capacity
   546	    // when increased to maximum possible columns can always support at
   547	    // least one row in memory.
   548	    //
   549	    // IF THIS EVER FAILS: We probably need to modify our logic below
   550	    // to reduce other elements of the capacity (styles, graphemes, etc.).
   551	    // But, instead, I recommend taking a step back and re-evaluating
   552	    // life choices.
   553	    comptime {
   554	        var cap = std_capacity;
   555	        cap.cols = std.math.maxInt(size.CellCountInt);
   556	        const layout = Page.layout(cap);
   557	        assert(layout.total_size <= size.max_page_size);
   558	    }
   559	
   560	    if (std_capacity.adjust(
   561	        .{ .cols = cols },
   562	    )) |cap| {
   563	        // If we can adjust our standard capacity, we fit within the
   564	        // standard size and we're good!
   565	        return cap;
   566	    } else |err| {
   567	        // Ensure our error set doesn't change.
   568	        comptime assert(@TypeOf(err) == error{OutOfMemory});
   569	    }
   570	
   571	    // This code path means that our standard capacity can't even
   572	    // accommodate our column count! The only solution is to increase
   573	    // our capacity and go non-standard.
   574	    var cap: Capacity = std_capacity;
   575	    cap.cols = cols;
   576	    return cap;
   577	}

   543	fn initialCapacity(cols: size.CellCountInt) Capacity {
   544	    // This is an important invariant that ensures that this function
   545	    // can never return an error. We verify here that our standard capacity
   546	    // when increased to maximum possible columns can always support at
   547	    // least one row in memory.
   548	    //
   549	    // IF THIS EVER FAILS: We probably need to modify our logic below
   550	    // to reduce other elements of the capacity (styles, graphemes, etc.).
   551	    // But, instead, I recommend taking a step back and re-evaluating
   552	    // life choices.
   553	    comptime {
   554	        var cap = std_capacity;
   555	        cap.cols = std.math.maxInt(size.CellCountInt);
   556	        const layout = Page.layout(cap);
   557	        assert(layout.total_size <= size.max_page_size);
   558	    }

   560	    if (std_capacity.adjust(
   561	        .{ .cols = cols },
   562	    )) |cap| {

   564	        // standard size and we're good!
   565	        return cap;

   572	    // accommodate our column count! The only solution is to increase
   573	    // our capacity and go non-standard.
   574	    var cap: Capacity = std_capacity;
   575	    cap.cols = cols;

   535	/// Calculates the initial capacity for a new page for a given column
   536	/// count. This will attempt to fit within std_size at all times so we
   537	/// can use our memory pool, but if cols is too big, this will return a
   538	/// larger capacity.
   539	///
   540	/// The returned capacity is always guaranteed to layout properly (not
   541	/// overflow). We are able to support capacities up to the maximum int
   542	/// value of cols, so this will never overflow.
   543	fn initialCapacity(cols: size.CellCountInt) Capacity {
   544	    // This is an important invariant that ensures that this function
   545	    // can never return an error. We verify here that our standard capacity
   546	    // when increased to maximum possible columns can always support at
   547	    // least one row in memory.
   548	    //
   549	    // IF THIS EVER FAILS: We probably need to modify our logic below
   550	    // to reduce other elements of the capacity (styles, graphemes, etc.).
   551	    // But, instead, I recommend taking a step back and re-evaluating
   552	    // life choices.
   553	    comptime {
   554	        var cap = std_capacity;
   555	        cap.cols = std.math.maxInt(size.CellCountInt);
   556	        const layout = Page.layout(cap);
   557	        assert(layout.total_size <= size.max_page_size);
   558	    }
   559	
   560	    if (std_capacity.adjust(
   561	        .{ .cols = cols },
   562	    )) |cap| {
   563	        // If we can adjust our standard capacity, we fit within the
   564	        // standard size and we're good!
   565	        return cap;
   566	    } else |err| {
   567	        // Ensure our error set doesn't change.
   568	        comptime assert(@TypeOf(err) == error{OutOfMemory});
   569	    }
   570	
   571	    // This code path means that our standard capacity can't even
   572	    // accommodate our column count! The only solution is to increase
   573	    // our capacity and go non-standard.
   574	    var cap: Capacity = std_capacity;
   575	    cap.cols = cols;
   576	    return cap;
   577	}

   535	/// Calculates the initial capacity for a new page for a given column
   536	/// count. This will attempt to fit within std_size at all times so we
   537	/// can use our memory pool, but if cols is too big, this will return a
   538	/// larger capacity.
   539	///
   540	/// The returned capacity is always guaranteed to layout properly (not
   541	/// overflow). We are able to support capacities up to the maximum int
   542	/// value of cols, so this will never overflow.
   543	fn initialCapacity(cols: size.CellCountInt) Capacity {
   544	    // This is an important invariant that ensures that this function
   545	    // can never return an error. We verify here that our standard capacity
   546	    // when increased to maximum possible columns can always support at
   547	    // least one row in memory.
   548	    //
   549	    // IF THIS EVER FAILS: We probably need to modify our logic below
   550	    // to reduce other elements of the capacity (styles, graphemes, etc.).
   551	    // But, instead, I recommend taking a step back and re-evaluating
   552	    // life choices.
   553	    comptime {
   554	        var cap = std_capacity;
   555	        cap.cols = std.math.maxInt(size.CellCountInt);
   556	        const layout = Page.layout(cap);
   557	        assert(layout.total_size <= size.max_page_size);
   558	    }
   559	
   560	    if (std_capacity.adjust(
   561	        .{ .cols = cols },
   562	    )) |cap| {
   563	        // If we can adjust our standard capacity, we fit within the
   564	        // standard size and we're good!
   565	        return cap;
   566	    } else |err| {
   567	        // Ensure our error set doesn't change.
   568	        comptime assert(@TypeOf(err) == error{OutOfMemory});
   569	    }
   570	
   571	    // This code path means that our standard capacity can't even
   572	    // accommodate our column count! The only solution is to increase
   573	    // our capacity and go non-standard.
   574	    var cap: Capacity = std_capacity;
   575	    cap.cols = cols;
   576	    return cap;
   577	}

   332	/// The returned terminal owns its memory. Call `deinit` with the same
   333	/// allocator when you are done with it.
   334	///
   335	/// ```zig

   341	/// happens before anything is allocated. If the size comes from an

   343	/// it yourself.
   344	pub fn init(
   345	    io_impl: std.Io,
   346	    alloc: Allocator,
   347	    opts: Options,
   348	) !Terminal {
   349	    const cols = opts.cols;
   350	    const rows = opts.rows;
   351	
   352	    // The screens and scrolling region need at least one row and column.
   353	    // Check this before allocating so there is nothing to clean up.
   354	    if (cols == 0 or rows == 0) return error.InvalidValue;
   355

   361	        .kitty_image_storage_limit = opts.kitty_image_storage_limit,
   362	        .kitty_image_loading_limits = opts.kitty_image_loading_limits,
   363	    });

   369	        .screens = screen_set,

  4920	    // Validate before changing any terminal state.

  4924	    // resize attempt, including one that doesn't change the grid dimensions.
  4925	    // Save their old values so later allocation failures can roll them back.
  4926	    const old_width_px = self.width_px;
  4927	    const old_height_px = self.height_px;
  4928	    const old_synchronized_output = self.modes.get(.synchronized_output);

  4930	        self.width_px = old_width_px;
  4931	        self.height_px = old_height_px;

   535	/// Calculates the initial capacity for a new page for a given column
   536	/// count. This will attempt to fit within std_size at all times so we
   537	/// can use our memory pool, but if cols is too big, this will return a
   538	/// larger capacity.
   539	///
   540	/// The returned capacity is always guaranteed to layout properly (not
   541	/// overflow). We are able to support capacities up to the maximum int
   542	/// value of cols, so this will never overflow.
   543	fn initialCapacity(cols: size.CellCountInt) Capacity {
   544	    // This is an important invariant that ensures that this function
   545	    // can never return an error. We verify here that our standard capacity
   546	    // when increased to maximum possible columns can always support at
   547	    // least one row in memory.
   548	    //
   549	    // IF THIS EVER FAILS: We probably need to modify our logic below
   550	    // to reduce other elements of the capacity (styles, graphemes, etc.).
   551	    // But, instead, I recommend taking a step back and re-evaluating
   552	    // life choices.
   553	    comptime {
   554	        var cap = std_capacity;
   555	        cap.cols = std.math.maxInt(size.CellCountInt);
   556	        const layout = Page.layout(cap);
   557	        assert(layout.total_size <= size.max_page_size);
   558	    }
   559	
   560	    if (std_capacity.adjust(
   561	        .{ .cols = cols },
   562	    )) |cap| {
   563	        // If we can adjust our standard capacity, we fit within the
   564	        // standard size and we're good!
   565	        return cap;
   566	    } else |err| {
   567	        // Ensure our error set doesn't change.
   568	        comptime assert(@TypeOf(err) == error{OutOfMemory});
   569	    }
   570	
   571	    // This code path means that our standard capacity can't even
   572	    // accommodate our column count! The only solution is to increase
   573	    // our capacity and go non-standard.
   574	    var cap: Capacity = std_capacity;
   575	    cap.cols = cols;
   576	    return cap;
   577	}
